set: Related services and edge cases (SLI, mild ID, 504, MTSS, CICO/safety)
disclaimer: Fictional synthetic exemplars for drafting practice only. No real student data. Not legal advice. Document types are labeled per exemplar.

exemplars.title: Grade 2 — Speech-Language Impairment, articulation/phonology
exemplars.profile_summary: A second-grade student whose speech is understood by familiar listeners about 70% of the time but by unfamiliar listeners about 50%; multiple sound errors persist past the expected age and affect phonemic awareness and early spelling.
strengths: Strong social confidence and willing to speak
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent reports the student gets frustrated when others cannot understand and worries about reading and spelling effects.
evaluation_data: Articulation/phonology assessment: errors on /r/, /s/ blends, /th/, and final consonants
Intelligibility: 70% familiar listeners, 50% unfamiliar
Phonological awareness and spelling errors align with speech error patterns
Adverse educational impact documented; SLI eligibility determined

plaafp.academic: The student reads at grade level with support but spelling and phonemic-awareness tasks show errors related to speech sound patterns; oral reading intelligibility drops with words containing target sounds.
plaafp.functional: The student is understood about 70% of the time by familiar listeners and 50% by unfamiliar listeners; sometimes repeats or avoids words with /r/ and /th/.
plaafp.impact: Speech sound errors related to the speech-language impairment reduce intelligibility in academic discussions and affect spelling/phonemic awareness development, requiring speech-language services and classroom supports.

goals.condition: During structured speech sessions and classroom speaking tasks
goals.skill: produce /r/, /s/ blends, and /th/ accurately in words, phrases, and connected speech
goals.target: 90% accuracy in words, 80% in phrases/sentences, and 75% in conversation across 3 consecutive sessions
goals.measurement: Articulation probes and spontaneous speech samples

goals.condition: Given classroom spelling and phonemic-awareness tasks containing target sounds
goals.skill: apply speech sound knowledge to spelling and decoding
goals.measurement: Classroom spelling checks and decoding probes

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with articulation probe data and classroom spelling samples.
supplementary_aids_services: Visual sound cues on the desk
Wait time to allow self-correction without interrupting meaning
Pre-teaching of speaking tasks containing target sounds
accommodations: Allow extra response time in oral activities
Do not penalize spelling errors related to target sounds while intervention is active
Opportunities for small-group speaking before whole-class sharing
personnel_supports: Teacher coaching on sound cues and positive correction
Scheduling coordination so speech does not conflict with core reading
exemplars.lre_statement: The student remains in general education for the full day except pull-out speech sessions. Pull-out is needed for individualized sound production practice with feedback; carryover supports are provided in the classroom so speech does not reduce access to core instruction.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out speech services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: District assessments with normal accommodations for speech; the student is not penalized for intelligibility issues in oral responses. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student has a history of regression in target sound accuracy over long breaks; ESY speech 2x/week for 30 minutes for 5 weeks is recommended based on regression/recoupment data. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Articulation-only SLI; the tool must track extra speech service dimensions and dismissal criteria.

exemplars.title: Grade 6 — Speech-Language Impairment, pragmatics/social language
exemplars.profile_summary: A sixth-grade student with average language skills in structure and vocabulary but significant difficulty with pragmatics — misunderstanding jokes/figurative language, interrupting, and misreading social situations — which affects peer relationships and group work.
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent reports the student feels left out and is often misunderstood by peers even though language testing looks 'fine.'
evaluation_data: Core language: average for grammar and vocabulary
Pragmatic language: below age expectations on informal and formal measures (topic maintenance, indirect language, repair)
Observation: interrupts peers, misses sarcasm/figurative language, difficulty negotiating
SLI eligibility determined for pragmatic language; adverse educational impact documented

plaafp.academic: The student writes and comprehends literal text at grade level but misinterprets figurative language and character motivation in literature; group-work grades suffer from difficulty negotiating roles and missing social cues.
plaafp.functional: The student struggles with turn-taking, initiating/ending conversations, and repairing communication breakdowns; 1–2 successful peer interactions per day; peers sometimes avoid group work with the student.
plaafp.impact: Pragmatic language deficits related to the speech-language impairment interfere with collaborative learning and peer relationships, requiring direct social-language instruction and classroom supports.

baselines.score: 2–3 turns before interruption or topic shift

goals.condition: During structured peer conversations and group work
goals.skill: take turns, maintain topic, and repair communication breakdowns
goals.target: 5+ turns with repair strategies in 8/10 opportunities across 3 consecutive sessions
goals.measurement: SLP language sample and observation checklist

goals.condition: Given literature and classroom discussion containing figurative or indirect language
goals.skill: interpret and respond appropriately to figurative/indirect language

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with SLP data and group-work teacher reports.

services.location: Speech room and push-in group work

supplementary_aids_services: Group roles with clear written expectations
Explicit pre-teaching of figurative language in upcoming texts
Structured opportunities for successful peer interaction (club/small group)
accommodations: Option to prepare responses in advance
Reduced penalty for off-topic contributions while skills are taught
personnel_supports: Teacher training on pragmatic language and inclusive group-work structures
SLP/ELA teacher co-planning on figurative language units
exemplars.lre_statement: The student is fully included in general education with push-in support during group work and pull-out pragmatic instruction. Push-in is intentional to practice social language in natural settings; pull-out provides explicit instruction that cannot be delivered incidentally.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out speech services and push-in supports (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time and small-group setting; figurative language items previewed per policy. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student showed regression in pragmatic skills over summer with slow recoupment; ESY social-language group 2x/week for 30 minutes is recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Distinguish from autism: pragmatic-only SLI with average core language. Useful for the category decision tree.

exemplars.title: Grade 4 — Mild Intellectual Disability, adaptive and academic skills
exemplars.profile_summary: A fourth-grade student with mild intellectual disability who reads at a first-to-second-grade level, solves one-step addition/subtraction with manipulatives, and needs support with daily living, safety, and social skills; participates meaningfully in general education with modifications.
strengths: Warm and social with peers and staff
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent wants the student to gain independence at home and be included with grade-level peers for social experiences.
evaluation_data: Cognitive assessment: significantly below average range; adaptive behavior deficits across conceptual, social, and practical domains
Academic achievement: reading and math well below grade level
Adaptive behavior scales completed by parent and teacher confirmed needs in daily living and safety
Mild intellectual disability eligibility determined

plaafp.academic: The student reads CVC and simple sight words at a first-to-second-grade level, writes one sentence with support, and solves one-step addition/subtraction within 20 using manipulatives. Grade-level fourth-grade content is accessed through modified materials.
plaafp.functional: The student needs prompting for personal organization, money/coin identification, safety awareness (e.g., crossing streets, unsafe situations), and following multi-step routines; social skills are a relative strength but reading social boundaries needs support.
plaafp.impact: Intellectual and adaptive-skill needs related to the disability require modified grade-level content, explicit functional/life-skills instruction, and substantial supports to participate in general education and community settings.

goals.condition: Given explicit instruction and community/school environmental print
goals.skill: read and use functional sight words
goals.target: 100 words with automaticity across 3 consecutive checks
goals.measurement: Sight-word inventory and environmental print checks

goals.condition: Given coins/bills and a classroom store routine
goals.skill: identify money, make amounts, and complete a purchase with the correct total
goals.target: 9/10 coins and independent purchase in 4/5 opportunities
goals.measurement: Functional math probes and classroom-store data

goals.condition: Given visual task lists and a consistent routine
goals.skill: complete morning/daily routines and identify safe/unsafe situations
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

benchmarks_or_stos: Break long-term goals into shorter objectives as required for alternate-assessment eligibility review.
exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with task-analysis data and functional probes; parent communication weekly via home-school notebook.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: No behavior concerns beyond needing routine and prompts; communication supports and AT considered below.

services.type: Special education — functional academics and life skills (SDI)
Special education — inclusion support in general education
services.provider: Special education paraprofessional under teacher direction

supplementary_aids_services: Modified grade-level materials and visual task lists
Peer buddies/peer supports in general education
Assistive technology for communication and organization
accommodations: Extended time and reduced work volume
program_modifications: Modified curriculum and reduced content for mastery in academic areas
Modified grading scale aligned to IEP goals
Alternative assignments focused on functional application of grade-level topics
personnel_supports: General education teacher collaboration on modifications
exemplars.lre_statement: The student participates in general education for science/social studies and specials with peer supports and modified materials, and receives explicit functional-academics SDI in the life-skills/resource setting. Pull-out is necessary for intensive, repetitive functional instruction; inclusion time is maximized for social and content exposure.
exemplars.placement: General education with substantial pull-out resource/life-skills services (outside regular class 21–60%).
exemplars.assessment: Team will review alternate-assessment eligibility criteria; for now participates in AASA with modifications as permitted. MOWR third-grade requirements were addressed in prior year.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student has documented severe regression in functional and academic skills over summer with slow recoupment and is at risk of losing safety/independence skills; ESY 3x/week for 60 minutes is recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
source_lineage: Missouri DESE example IEP A (ID, structure only)
exemplars.notes: Only mild-ID exemplar in the set; includes modified grading and alternate-assessment consideration. The tool should trigger the benchmarks/STOs rule when alternate assessment may apply.

exemplars.title: Grade 5 — Section 504 plan (not an IEP): ADHD accommodations
exemplars.az_category: Not applicable — Section 504 (ADHD, does not require specially designed instruction)
exemplars.profile_summary: A fifth-grade student with ADHD who does not require specially designed instruction; the team determined that a 504 accommodation plan is the appropriate vehicle for access (reduced-distraction testing, movement breaks, extended time).
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent wants accommodations in place but does not want the student pulled out of class.
evaluation_data: Medical diagnosis of ADHD
Section 504 eligibility: physical/mental impairment substantially limiting a major life activity (learning, concentrating)
No need for specially designed instruction documented; all academic skills are at or above grade level with accommodations
IEP team considered special education and determined it is not necessary; 504 plan developed

plaafp.academic: The student performs at grade level with accommodations and completes 85% of work; no SDI is needed. Attention and test performance improve with movement breaks and a low-distraction setting.
plaafp.functional: Impulsivity during tests and long tasks; benefits from seated breaks, check-ins, and chunking.
plaafp.impact: ADHD symptoms affect access to instruction and testing but not the need for specially designed instruction; accommodations provide equitable access.

goals.area: Accommodation monitoring (504 review, not IEP goals)
goals.skill: access instruction and testing without a need for special education
goals.target: 95% completion and continued grade-level performance at the annual 504 review
goals.schedule: Progress monitored each marking period; annual 504 review

exemplars.progress_reporting: Each marking period, with an annual review of 504 eligibility and accommodations.
accommodations: Extended time on tests and assignments
personnel_supports: Staff awareness of 504 plan and accommodation delivery
exemplars.lre_statement: Not applicable to a 504 plan; the student accesses general education with accommodations and is not removed from class.
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with 504-approved accommodations (extended time, low-distraction setting, breaks).
exemplars.esy: Not applicable to a 504 plan; no ESY services.
source_lineage: AZ-TAS 2025 (special education vs. general education), ADA/Section 504 regulations
exemplars.notes: Contrast exemplar. The tool should force the IEP-vs-504 decision before drafting: no SDI = 504 path. Must NOT generate IEP goals for this student.

exemplars.title: Grade 3 — MTSS pre-referral documentation (not an IEP): reading intervention data
exemplars.az_category: Not applicable — general education MTSS (documentation toward possible referral)
exemplars.profile_summary: A third-grade student receiving Tier 2/3 reading intervention whose data show insufficient progress after 12 weeks of evidence-based instruction. This record documents the intervention, fidelity, and progress before a special education referral decision.
strengths: Early literacy team member is committed to data collection
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent is worried about reading progress and has met with the teacher twice.
evaluation_data: Universal screening: grade-3 reading at the 12th percentile (fall and winter)
Diagnostic: letter-sound and blending gaps; phonemic awareness below grade level
Intervention: 12 weeks of explicit phonics intervention, 4x/week, 30 min, delivered by trained interventionist
Progress data: 8 data points showing a flat/table-low line; fidelity checks completed weekly at 90%+
Educational impact: reading gaps affect all content areas; referral to special education under consideration

plaafp.academic: Despite 12 weeks of evidence-based Tier 2/3 phonics intervention with high fidelity, the student reads 32 WCPM and shows no reliable progress trend (slope near zero) on weekly probes; universal screening is at the 12th percentile.
plaafp.functional: The student works hard in intervention, but frustration behaviors (head down, refusal) increase during extended reading tasks; attendance is consistent.
plaafp.impact: Reading difficulty is not responding as expected to high-quality instruction, and the team is now reviewing whether a disability-related need exists that requires special education.

baselines.score: 32 WCPM with a near-zero slope over 8 points

goals.area: MTSS intervention goal (not an IEP goal)
goals.skill: improve phonemic awareness and oral reading fluency
goals.baseline: 32 WCPM; phonemic awareness below grade level
goals.target: Student will gain at least 1.0 words/week slope over the next 6 weeks; if not, the team will consider a special education referral
goals.measurement: Weekly CBM probes and fidelity checks

exemplars.progress_reporting: MTSS team meets every 6 weeks; parent receives written data updates.
exemplars.lre_statement: Not applicable — this is a general education intervention document. The student remains in the general education classroom and receives intervention as a general education support.
exemplars.placement: General education with MTSS Tier 2/3 intervention.
exemplars.assessment: Participates in universal screening and state assessments without an IEP; no accommodations beyond standard classroom supports.
source_lineage: PBIS Tier 3 Brief FBA Guide (progress-monitoring framing)
exemplars.notes: Shows how documentation of appropriate instruction and progress monitoring matters for SLD eligibility (A.R.S. §15-761 determinant factors). The tool should be able to produce this pre-referral record.

exemplars.title: Grade 5 — Check-in/Check-out and safety plan (Tier 2 behavior support; not a full IEP)
exemplars.az_category: General education behavior support (student also has an IEP — this plan is attached to it)
exemplars.profile_summary: A fifth-grade student with an existing IEP who responds well to adult attention and frequent feedback; the team added a check-in/check-out (CICO) plan with a safety plan for hallway transitions after two unsafe incidents.
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent wants daily feedback and consistency across home and school.
evaluation_data: FBA update: behavior functions include adult attention and escape from non-preferred transitions
CICO data from a 4-week trial: on-task and safety increased when points were available
Two unsafe hallway incidents (leaving the line, entering staff areas) prompted a safety plan
IEP team amended the behavior plan without a full meeting by written agreement

plaafp.academic: The student completes 75% of work on CICO days versus 55% on non-CICO days; reading and math are at grade level with support.
plaafp.functional: The student seeks adult attention and struggles during unstructured transitions; CICO has improved regulation and hallway safety.
plaafp.impact: Attention-seeking and transition-escape behavior reduce instructional time; structured adult feedback and a safety plan improve access and safety.

goals.condition: With CICO points and a transition safety routine
goals.skill: follow transition expectations and remain with the group
goals.target: 9/10 safe transitions and 85% CICO points across 6 consecutive weeks
goals.measurement: Daily point card and transition tallies
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

exemplars.progress_reporting: Daily point card sent home; weekly data summary; quarterly IEP progress report.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Behavior support attached to the IEP; CICO and safety plan implemented and monitored.
supplementary_aids_services: Daily point card with 3 targeted expectations
Reinforcement menu (school store, extra recess, helper roles)
accommodations: Extended time on assignments when behavior interrupted work
personnel_supports: Mentor training on CICO and data collection
Para/hallway staff briefing on safety plan
exemplars.lre_statement: The student remains in general education with CICO and safety supports; no removal is planned. Pull-out is limited to explicit behavior/SEL instruction.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: Existing IEP assessment accommodations apply; CICO continues during testing week with breaks.
exemplars.esy: Existing IEP ESY consideration applies; no additional ESY needed for behavior.

behavior_support_plan.target_behavior_operational: Leaving the transition line, entering restricted areas, and attention-seeking interruptions during transitions.
behavior_support_plan.hypothesized_function: Access to adult attention; escape from unstructured/non-preferred transitions.
antecedent_strategies: Assign a leadership role in line (helper)
Preview transition expectations with a visual
replacement_behaviors_taught: Stay with the group and use a hand signal to get attention
Ask the teacher a question at an appropriate time
Self-monitor point card and set a daily goal
consequence_strategies: Points and specific praise for safe transitions and CICO goals
Neutral redirection; reteach expectation; unsafe hallway behavior triggers a supervised transition until 10 consecutive safe transitions
behavior_support_plan.crisis_plan: If the student leaves the group and enters an unsafe area, staff use the safety-plan script: remain calm, block access to unsafe areas without physical restraint unless imminent danger, contact the office, and notify the parent same day if safety was compromised. Any restraint/seclusion follows A.R.S. §15-105 and triggers a team review.
behavior_support_plan.progress_monitoring: Daily point card, transition tallies, weekly team review, monthly FBA/BIP check.
staff_responsibilities: Teachers: point card and transition supports
Case manager: data and family communication
Behavior team: data review and plan adjustments

source_lineage: PBIS Basic FBA to BSP and Tier 3 Brief Guide
exemplars.notes: Illustrates CICO + safety plan as an amendment to an existing IEP; different from a full IEP exemplar by design.
